observation_summary: The compiler fails to process @lends annotations when the class being lent to is defined in the same statement as the @lends annotation, resulting in an 'not declared before @lends annotation' error.
hypothesis: The compiler's type inference logic processes object literals with @lends annotations immediately, before the symbol they are lending to has been fully defined in the scope. The fix requires deferring the processing of these object literals until the statement containing the definition is fully parsed.
prediction: The code will introduce a mechanism to collect object literals with @lends annotations during the initial traversal and process them only after the statement has been fully analyzed.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the introduction of a 'lentObjectLiterals' list to store object literals with @lends annotations, and logic to process these literals only after the statement is parsed. This confirms that the original algorithm was too eager in its processing, failing to account for the order of definition within a single statement.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic issue where the compiler's processing order for @lends annotations was incorrect. It attempted to resolve the target of the @lends before the target was defined in the same statement. The fix involves changing the procedural logic (the algorithm) to defer the processing of these specific nodes until the statement is complete. This is a classic procedural/algorithmic correction rather than a simple value assignment or a missing guard check.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows the addition of a 'lentObjectLiterals' list and logic to defer 'defineObjectLiteral(objLit)' calls until after the statement is processed.
The bug report states that @lends does not work when the class is defined in the same statement, confirming the issue is related to the order of operations/processing logic.
The failing tests confirm that the compiler incorrectly reports that the prototype is not declared, which is a direct consequence of the premature processing of the @lends annotation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves managing the relationship between the @lends annotation and the class definition, the root cause is the procedural order of operations (the algorithm) used by the compiler to process these nodes.
This is not a missing design capability; the feature exists, but the implementation of the processing algorithm was flawed regarding the order of operations.
